label: rust-anything pins its lint policy inside the single crate's own manifest ([lints.rust] unsafe_code = forbid, [lints.clippy] all = warn priority -1); the sk-code Rust set shows only the workspace form [workspace.lints.rust] and never a single-crate [lints.*] block, so an app-style crate has no template.

rust-anything declares edition 2024 and rust-version 1.97 and reads the MSRV back as a compile-time constant via env!("CARGO_PKG_RUST_VERSION") in src/lib.rs, so the declared MSRV is the single source of truth; sk-code covers the declaration but lacks the single-source pattern.

rust-anything is a single crate with a lib+bin split: src/lib.rs declares 69 pub mod items plus two private modules and src/main.rs is a thin front end importing the library; the sk-code set's only layout is a five-crate workspace whose binary lives in a separate sidecar crate, so a single-crate CLI app has no layout template.

rust-anything uses anyhow at every layer (54 of 74 src files import it, 462 bail!/context/with_context sites, no thiserror dependency), which sk-code's P0 rule 'Do not use anyhow in pure-core public APIs or exported functions' and its P1 checklist 'Core errors use typed thiserror enums' would flag as a violation; the contradiction is a scope gap, not a sk-code error, because the rule is written for a binding core consumed by adapters.

rust-anything configures serde_json with float_roundtrip, preserve_order and unbounded_depth so recorded floats survive parsing bit for bit; sk-code warns that serde_json does not match JavaScript number spelling but never names the float_roundtrip feature that remedies it.

rust-anything applies a uniform serde attribute convention: rename_all = kebab-case on report enums, skip_serializing_if on optional and empty fields, serde(default) on forward-compatible input fields, and deny_unknown_fields on the config struct; the sk-code Rust set has zero hits for deny_unknown_fields, skip_serializing_if or rename_all.

rust-anything's clap CLI is derive-first: #[derive(Parser)] with #[command(name, version, about, after_help)], a #[derive(Subcommand)] enum whose variant doc comments become help text, ValueEnum for closed sets, and #[arg(default_value = ".")] on the root positional; the sk-code Rust set has zero hits for clap, so CLI argument design is entirely absent.

rust-anything's test layout is 46 top-level tests/*.rs integration files, one shared tests/common/mod.rs helper module and 30 fixture directories under tests/fixtures/; sk-code covers tests/*.rs and tests/common/mod.rs but has zero hits for tests/fixtures, so the fixture-tree convention is absent.

rust-anything's CLAUDE.md finish gate is cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test, and update docs/STATUS.md when what works changed; sk-code carries the clippy form but has no rule that a behaviour-changing edit must update a status document.
